Skyline to share top 12 accounts for mapping and contact emails by 2025-05-14
Diego to draft integration checklist and light benchmark run plan by 2025-05-16

meeting_header:
Date: 2025-05-09
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Amelia Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood Partner Ops), Ravi Patel (Skyline Head of Alliances), Marta Liu (Skyline Channel Development), Jonas Kline (Skyline Director Cloud Partnerships), Samir Gupta (Skyline SE)
summary: Partner-led referral pipeline sprint: align GTM plays, map top accounts, outline co-sell/referral motions, and agree on lightweight bench for high-fit accounts. Discussed mutual enablement, legal/ops gating, and potential competitor motion intercepts.
topics: ops and legal gating (SLA/KPI, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00] Amelia Park: Okay, um, thanks everyone for joining. Quick roll call — we got Skyline folks, Redwood folks. Uh, objective today is a sprint to map accounts and agree referral flows, right?
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Yep that's right, thanks Amelia. We want a lightweight process, ideally something our field reps can use without long procurement cycles.
[00:25] Marta Liu: Hi all — quick note, some of our reps keep asking about pricing and handoffs, so we'd like a simple tracker.
[00:33] Diego Morales: Makes sense. I can show a sample tracker Diego, sorry, I mean, I can show a sample tracker and the suggested play template — won't share screen now, we'll attach after.
[00:44] Jonas Kline: On prioritization — we have a set of accounts in EMEA where latency is critical; they always ask about VPC or on-prem options. Should we pre-qualify for Redwood Private or Dedicated?
[00:58] Amelia Park: Good question. For the sprint let's mark them as "privacy-sensitive" and push them for an SE follow-up. We can propose a Preferred Play: hosted first, then offer Dedicated for pilot customers that need predictability.
[01:12] Samir Gupta: Quick clarifying — when you say "Dedicated" do you mean reserved capacity or a managed private instance? Customers sometimes confuse the two.
[01:22] Priya Shah: We'll note terminology in the one-pager. For the tracker we should have a dropdown: hosted / dedicated / private.
[01:31] Ravi Patel: Also to call out compliance — a few accounts require SOC 2 Type II evidence and audit logs for third-party calls. Is Redwood ok with that?
[01:42] Amelia Park: Yes, Redwood provides SOC 2 artifacts, KMS integration, and audit logs for Private and Dedicated. We'll attach the security pack.
[01:52] Marta Liu: Awesome. Can you also flag data residency? A handful of EU customers need regional processing.
[02:01] Diego Morales: We'll include region tags. There might be a small latency delta for EU region Wirings but it's usually within SLA if pinned.
[02:11] Ravi Patel: Cool. Moving on — mapping. We've got a rough list of 20 accounts. For the sprint we suggested picking top 12 where we can land a referral or 2-week POC.
[02:25] Jonas Kline: 12 sounds right. We should score by fit: cloud maturity, use-case fit, procurement timeline.
[02:33] Amelia Park: Let's use a simple 1-5 scoring on three axes: fit, timeline (procurement), and enablement difficulty. We can share that sheet.
[02:45] [Crosstalk] Marta Liu: — I can take the lead on gathering rep feedback —
[02:49] Amelia Park: Great, Marta on rep feedback. Diego, can you outline a tiny benchmark we can run to reassure ops teams?
[02:57] Diego Morales: Sure. Minimal bench: run a 5k-token generative prompt at representative concurrency — say 4 concurrent sessions — measure p95 latency and token cost. Use both hosted and a quantized Dedicated variant. I want to caveat — quantization numbers vary by model.
[03:18] Samir Gupta: Is there a way to simulate customer's token distribution?
[03:22] Diego Morales: Yes, ideally Skyline provides a short corpus and sample prompts. We'll run with that.
[03:27] Ravi Patel: We can do that. Also, we have a concern about routing — some of our accounts route to EU regional endpoints only. How do we handle fallback if capacity is limited?
[03:39] Amelia Park: Redwood has smart routing — we can route by policy. For the sprint we'll recommend a fallback policy: primary region, then compatible model in other region, then reduced-batch fallback to keep latency low. We'll include that flow in the doc.
[03:54] Marta Liu: Are there costs we should warn reps about when recommending Dedicated?
[03:58] Amelia Park: Yes, Dedicated is a committed cost. The tracker should show expected unit economics: token cost delta, baseline hosted price, and approximate monthly commit. We'll put ballpark numbers but mark as provisional.
[04:13] Jonas Kline: On the legal side — we need a standard MSA addendum for referrals, plus an SLA on lead follow-up time. Do you have a recommended cadence?
[04:24] Priya Shah: We usually propose 48 business hours to accept or handoff a referral; and a 30-day nurture window to log status. Legal can give a short addendum.
[04:35] Ravi Patel: That 48-hour SLA is important to our reps.
[04:38] Amelia Park: We'll put the SLA into the one-pager. Also, we should define how revenue credit is split for co-sell influenced deals — maybe a simple points system for this sprint.
[04:50] Marta Liu: Points system is fine for now. We can formalize in the next iteration.
[04:54] Diego Morales: Quick tech note — some accounts will insist on on-prem kernel compatibility. We should surface that as a red flag and push for an SE-led pilot.
[05:05] Jonas Kline: Noted.
[05:08] [12:00] Amelia Park: Jumping ahead to timelines — we want the tracker and contacts by next Wednesday, and Redwood will return a filled mapping and bench plan by Friday. Does that align?
[12:18] Ravi Patel: That works if Legal isn't a blocker.
[12:22] Amelia Park: We'll mark legal as an early check — Priya, can you own getting Legal touchpoints?
[12:28] Priya Shah: Yep, I'll sync legal and pull a short MSA addendum template we use with partners.
[12:34] Marta Liu: A quick question about competitors — our field hears a lot about EpochAI and CloudFlux doing aggressive reseller plays. Any talking points?
[12:44] Amelia Park: For EpochAI we recommend focusing on predictable TCO and enterprise SLAs; for CloudFlux, emphasize integration velocity and the ability to run private deployments. I'll share two one-liners for reps.
[12:57] Samir Gupta: Also worth noting some accounts care more about inference speed than number of features. We should help reps surface that.
[13:05] Diego Morales: Agreed — we'll include a short playbook: latency-first vs cost-first customer signals and which model/config to pitch.
[13:15] Ravi Patel: Ok — about the referral form — do you have a lightweight API or should we just use Google forms for now?
[13:23] Amelia Park: For the sprint I'd suggest Google form or shared sheet to move fast; we can prototype an API integration later. The referral tracker will include fields for account name, contact, region, privacy flag, and recommended motion.
[13:36] Marta Liu: Good. We'll standardize naming conventions to avoid duplicates.
[13:40] Amelia Park: One more operational question — how do we credit revenue if Skyline's rep introduces and Redwood closes? We proposed a 20% referral fee in initial talks — is that still acceptable?
[13:53] Ravi Patel: It's within range, but we need to see legal language and a short revenue crediting process.
[13:58] Priya Shah: We'll draft the revenue credit flow and include in the one-pager — who owns the lead, how it's logged in CRM, and payout timing.
[14:08] Jonas Kline: On CRM — do we expect to push leads into our Salesforce or will Redwood create the opportunity? We need to avoid duplicate ownership.
[14:18] Amelia Park: Best practice is Skyline logs the lead in your Salesforce and tags Redwood as partner; Redwood will link via CRM-deal ID for reporting. We'll include mapping guidance.
[14:28] Ravi Patel: Sounds good.
[14:31] [20:02] Diego Morales: Back to tech: for the bench we'll measure p95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll run both 'vanilla' host model and a smaller quantized variant. Expect variance +/- 20% on token cost for quantized models depending on workload.
[20:42] Marta Liu: Will you need API keys?
[20:45] Diego Morales: Yes, if you want us to run on actual customer samples we need a short-lived key or sample corpus. We can also run on our internal baseline with similar prompts.
[20:56] Ravi Patel: We'll provide a sanitized sample corpus and a contact to hand over keys.
[21:02] Amelia Park: For the privacy-sensitive accounts, we do recommend a pilot in Dedicated or Private to show stability. We can scope a 6-week pilot with a clear rollback.
[21:14] Jonas Kline: Ok.
[21:16] [30:00] Marta Liu: Operationally, who will own day-to-day? I'm thinking Skyline field reps + a Redwood partner PM as escalation.
[30:08] Amelia Park: Yeah, Redwood will assign a partner PM for this sprint. Priya can be the ops liaison and Diego will cover SE escalations.
[30:19] Priya Shah: I'll set up a shared Slack channel and calendar invites for weekly syncs; suggest Tuesdays 14:00 UTC.
[30:28] Ravi Patel: Tuesdays works.
[30:31] [38:45] Samir Gupta: One more tech flag — some accounts run older transformer variants; they might ask about KV cache persistence and session continuity across nodes.
[38:58] Diego Morales: We support KV cache management, but we need to define session affinity in the bench. We'll add that as a variable.
[39:08] Marta Liu: Good call.
[39:11] Amelia Park: Let's recap actions: Amelia to send one-pager and tracker (due Mon 5/11), Marta to send top 12 accounts (due Wed 5/14), Diego to prepare bench plan (due Fri 5/16), Priya to create ops channel (due Sat 5/10). Any additions?
[39:31] Ravi Patel: None from me.
[39:34] Jonas Kline: All good.
[39:36] Amelia Park: Great — we'll also attach security docs and sample MSA addendum with the one-pager. If legal pushes back we'll triage in the next call.
[39:47] Marta Liu: Thanks everyone.
[39:49] Amelia Park: Thanks all, see you next week.
[39:52] [END]
